newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Informix calls heavily traded.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Informix calls heavily traded.

text.p: Volume in Informix Corp call options ballooned and implied volatilities soared as a conference the company was holding in California created a variety of speculation, traders said.
Informix August 12.5 calls were the most active contract on the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), with more than 8,800 contracts changing hands by 1230 CDT/1730 GMT.
September 12.5 calls and August 10.0 calls had turnover of more than 4,700, and the August 12.5 calls also traded heavily on the American Stock Exchange (AMEX).
The stock was up 1-1/16 at 10-3/4, also on hefty volume.

The surge in interest stemmed from a big user conference which Informix, a database technology firm, was holding in San Francisco, said strategist Paul Foster of Mercury Trading, a market-making firm at CBOE handling Informix options.
"It creates excitement when you have 6,000 programmers and users," he said. "Obviously, there are some money managers there."
Traders said talks and rumors driving up interest ranged from possible management changes, takeovers, earnings and future products.
"It's nothing specific," Foster said. "Implied volatilities have spiked up on anxiety over what actually is going on because I don't think anyone really knows what the issues are."
Implied volatility for the August 12.5 calls shot up to about 110 percent from usual levels near 70 percent.
Harrison Roth, first vice president of Cowen & Co, said the call buying looked mostly outright, not boosted by spreads.
Foster said the order flow was coming in from a "mixture of paper (retail customers)".

Time-and-sale figures showed that most orders came in small lots, indicating the public was buying, after a few large institutionals-size orders early in the session, said Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer & Co.

He noted that when implied volatilities were bid up in such a way, market makers tended to have an upper hand because volatilities would shrink after the speculative interest dried up, making it difficult for premiums to appreciate.
Still, most traders said the stock looked positive technically as it has broken out of a 1-1/2 month range between 8-1/2 and 10.
Elsewhere, International Business Machines Corp options saw heavy volume again after the company released its earnings late Monday.

Interestingly, Schwartz said, implied volatilities shrank drastically despite a pullback in the stock price. Thus, premium on August 100 puts, the vehicle of choice for stockholders hedging against a decline, was down 1 at 3-1/2.
"It didn't make sense to buy the puts yesterday," he said.
Jay Shartsis, director of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co, said the reaction probably meant the stock has put in a near-term bottom. IBM was off 1-9/16 at 102-1/8 in late trade.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
